subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and where should it draw the boundary between silent-intent text and legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves some substantive trailing-token replies while this issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks, so the right boundary is a maintainer security and message-delivery policy choice.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and applies consistently across delivery paths.

options.title: Suppress any trailing or own-line token
options.body: Treat every reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token as silent, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the current narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, JSON, reasoning-prefixed, and selected cron silent payloads are suppressed, then close or retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and applies consistently across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans shared reply delivery, security policy, and the current central-file history where steipete is the strongest routing candidate.
